{{Short description|Concept in differential geometry}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:''G''<sub>2</sub>-structure}}
{{Use American English|date = March 2019}}
In [[differential geometry]], a '''<math>G_2</math>-structure''' is an important type of [[G-structure]] that can be defined on a [[smooth manifold]].  If ''M'' is a smooth manifold of dimension seven, then a G<sub>2</sub>-structure is a reduction of structure group of the [[frame bundle]] of ''M'' to the [[compact group|compact]], exceptional [[Lie group]] [[G2 (mathematics)|G<sub>2</sub>]].

== Equivalent conditions ==
The existence of  a <math>G_2</math> structure on a 7-manifold <math>M</math> is equivalent to either of the following conditions:
*The first and second [[Stiefel–Whitney class]]es of ''M'' vanish.
*''M'' is [[orientable]] and admits a [[spin structure]].
It follows that the existence of a  <math>G_2</math>-structure is much weaker than the existence of a metric of holonomy <math>G_2</math>, because a compact 7-manifold of holonomy <math>G_2</math> must also  have finite fundamental group and  non-vanishing first [[Pontrjagin class]].

== History ==
The fact that there might be certain Riemannian 7-manifolds manifolds of holonomy <math>G_2</math> was first suggested by [[Marcel Berger]]'s 1955 classification of possible Riemannian holonomy groups.   Although still working in a complete absence of examples, [[Edmond Bonan]] then forged ahead in 1966, and investigated the properties that a manifold of holonomy <math>G_2</math> would necessarily have; in particular, he showed that such a manifold would carry a parallel 3-form and a parallel 4-form,  and that the manifold would necessarily be Ricci-flat.<ref>{{citation | last = E. Bonan | title = Sur les variétés riemanniennes à groupe d'holonomie G2 ou Spin(7)| journal = C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris | volume =262| year = 1966  | pages = 127&ndash;129}}.</ref> However, it remained unclear whether such metrics actually existed until [[Robert Bryant (mathematician)|Robert Bryant]]  proved a local  existence theorem for such metrics in 1984.  The first complete (although non-compact) 7-manifolds with holonomy <math>G_2</math> were constructed by Bryant and Simon Salamon in 1989.<ref>{{citation | last1 = Bryant | first1 = R.L. |author-link1 = Robert Bryant (mathematician) | first2 =  S.M. | last2 = Salamon | title = On the construction of some complete metrics with exceptional holonomy | journal = Duke Mathematical Journal | volume = 58 | year = 1989 | issue = 3 | pages = 829&ndash;850 | doi = 10.1215/s0012-7094-89-05839-0 }}.</ref> The first compact 7-manifolds with holonomy <math>G_2</math> were constructed by [[Dominic Joyce]] in 1994, and compact <math>G_2</math> manifolds are sometimes known as "Joyce manifolds", especially in the physics literature.<ref>{{citation | first = D.D. | last = Joyce | title = Compact Manifolds with Special Holonomy | series = Oxford Mathematical Monographs | publisher = Oxford University Press |  isbn = 0-19-850601-5 | year = 2000}}.</ref> In 2013, it was shown by M. Firat Arikan, Hyunjoo Cho, and Sema Salur that any manifold with a [[spin structure]], and, hence, a <math>G_2</math>-structure, admits a compatible almost contact metric structure, and an explicit compatible almost contact structure was constructed for manifolds with <math>G_2</math>-structure.<ref>{{citation | first1 = M. Firat | last1 = Arikan | first2 =  Hyunjoo | last2 = Cho | first3 =  Sema | last3 = Salur | title = Existence of compatible contact structures on <math>G_2</math>-manifolds | journal = Asian J. Math. | issue = 2 | volume = 17 | year = 2013  | pages = 321&ndash;334 | doi = 10.4310/AJM.2013.v17.n2.a3 | publisher = International Press of Boston| arxiv = 1112.2951 | s2cid = 54942812 }}.</ref> In the same paper, it was shown that certain classes of [[G2 manifold|<math>G_2</math>-manifolds]] admit a [[Contact geometry#Contact forms and structures|contact structure]].

== Remarks ==
The property of being a [[G2 manifold|<math>G_2</math>-manifold]] is much stronger than that of admitting a <math>G_2</math>-structure.  Indeed, being a <math>G_2</math>-manifold is equivalent to admitting a <math>G_2</math>-structure that is [[G-structure#Torsion of a G-structure|torsion-free]].

The letter "G" occurring in the phrases "G-structure" and "<math>G_2</math>-structure" refers to different things.  In the first case, G-structures take their name from the fact that arbitrary Lie groups are typically denoted with the letter "G".  On the other hand, the letter "G" in "<math>G_2</math>" comes from the fact that its Lie algebra is the seventh type ("G" being the seventh letter of the alphabet) in the classification of complex simple Lie algebras by [[Élie Cartan]].
